sourceEvidence.label: Public authentication, deployment, credentials, and logging review

assessment.summary: Public launch is blocked by disclosed credentials, client/dispersed authorization, and ineffective security telemetry.

nonNegotiables: Every business page and API is default-deny.
Known tracked credentials are rotated before public launch.
Replacement secrets are never written to source, logs, command arguments, or chat.
Local file rendering cannot create a remote HTTP bypass.
assumptions: No measured latency, memory, or retention budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Contain exposed credentials and bootstrap authority
opportunities.summary: Rotate disclosed values, remove Git as a secret transport, and replace predictable administrator bootstrap.
opportunities.diagnosis: Secret lifecycle ownership is dispersed across tracked files and scripts, leaving historical disclosure and predictable administrator authority.

evidence.claim: Tracked files and history contain non-placeholder provider, database, and signing credentials.
A read-only database check confirmed the active administrator still matched the known source default password.
Editing current files alone cannot revoke copies already distributed through Git history.

desiredInvariants: No deployable credential exists in distributed Git history after cleanup.
Every disclosed value is revoked at its authority provider.
Administrator bootstrap is one-time, interactive, non-default, and session-revoking.

options.title: Rotate and remove current files
options.summary: Rotate known values, reset the administrator, sanitize HEAD, and expand ignore rules.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Rotation invalidates inventoried values, but old history and recurrence controls remain.
Interactive reset removes the known administrator password.

tradeoffs.assessment: Stops reuse of every value covered by the rotation inventory but leaves historical copies and recurrence risk.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify former values fail at each provider and scan current refs.

tradeoffs.assessment: No request-path control is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm startup and request baselines are unchanged.

tradeoffs.assessment: No retained runtime structure is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: No dedicated benchmark beyond startup RSS comparison.

tradeoffs.assessment: Manual rotation can cause temporary provider outages if rollout order is wrong.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use dual-key overlap where supported and provider health checks.

tradeoffs.assessment: Provider-by-provider manual inventory and delivery are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require an owner and revocation receipt for each item.

tradeoffs.assessment: Small current-tree change, but no history migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Deploy from a sanitized checkout with replacement values.

residualRisks: Old commits and clones retain disclosed values.

acceptanceCriteria: All former values fail and no known default account password remains.
migrationNotes: Never restore revoked values during rollback.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore deployment topology only with newly generated values.

options.title: Managed secret lifecycle and history cleanup
options.summary: Add protected runtime injection, history rewrite, interactive bootstrap, and automated secret scanning.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Managed injection and history cleanup remove normal Git access while provider rotation remains mandatory.
One-time non-default bootstrap owns administrator creation and revocation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes Git authority, reduces historical exposure, and prevents predictable bootstrap recurrence.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Scan all refs, verify provider revocation, and test CI blocking.

tradeoffs.assessment: Secret retrieval occurs at deploy/start, outside normal requests.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure service startup with the secret store.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only a small secret-manager client and transient values are added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare startup RSS and ensure values are not retained unnecessarily.

tradeoffs.assessment: A secret-store dependency improves consistency but may block startup during outage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test fail-closed startup and recovery without a restart storm.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires secret-store ownership, rotation workflow, scanner triage, and clone coordination.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a full rotation and history-rewrite rehearsal.

tradeoffs.assessment: History rewrite disrupts clones and open branches.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use a maintenance window and require fresh-clone verification.

residualRisks: Uncontrolled clones, backups, and caches may retain old values.
Secret-manager administrator compromise remains high impact.

acceptanceCriteria: Old values fail, all refs scan clean, and clean deployment uses only managed injection.
migrationNotes: Coordinate forced history replacement with every collaborator.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Retain sanitized Git and use fresh local protected values if the manager must be rolled back.

opportunities.recommendation: Use managed secrets, with immediate provider rotation as the first work package.

opportunities.title: Centralize public authentication enforcement
opportunities.summary: Make pages and APIs default-deny, use revocable sessions, constrain login abuse, and close direct origins.
opportunities.diagnosis: Authorization is split between browser JavaScript and route opt-in decorators, while DEBUG and deployment paths create bypasses.

evidence.claim: Page access is enforced by browser JavaScript after static HTML delivery.
Static route inventory found 225 of 371 handlers without a known authentication decorator.
DEBUG mode substitutes administrator authority for anonymous requests.
Login/register lack active abuse controls and public registration is enabled.
Browser bearer tokens are stored in localStorage and are weakly revocable.
Backend and Redis host ports are published.
Wildcard credentialed CORS and raw forwarded headers make origin and identity assumptions drift.

desiredInvariants: All business pages and APIs are denied outside a minimal allowlist without a valid revocable session.
Dangerous operations require an explicit administrator role.
Production cannot start with DEBUG, development config, weak signing keys, or public internal services.
Login abuse is limited independently by trusted IP, account, and global state with MFA.

options.title: Application and Nginx session gate
options.summary: Use Flask default-deny, Nginx auth_request, Redis sessions and rate limits, secure cookies, CSRF, and private internal ports.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Nginx validates a server session before serving HTML.
Application policy becomes default-deny and privileged routes are classified.
DEBUG fallback is removed and production startup rejects unsafe config.
Registration closes and shared IP/account/global limits plus MFA protect login.
HttpOnly server sessions replace browser bearer storage and support revocation.
Internal services stop publishing public host ports.
Same-origin CORS and trusted-proxy handling become explicit.

tradeoffs.assessment: Eliminates known client, decorator, DEBUG, token-storage, and direct-port bypass classes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run anonymous/role route contracts, direct-port probes, CSRF, XSS-token, and revocation tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds Redis session lookup and an auth subrequest for protected HTML.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare p50/p95 login, page, and API latency with realistic concurrency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Redis retains bounded session and rate-limit state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure bytes per session and abuse-key cardinality at expected and attack loads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fail-closed Redis/session dependency can reduce availability while removing unsafe bypass behavior.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test Redis outage, restart, expiration, and recovery behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds session, CSRF, rate-limit, portal, Nginx auth, and role-policy ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise deployment, lockout recovery, and break-glass runbooks.

tradeoffs.assessment: Frontend bearer calls and automation clients need staged migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use dual-read compatibility, inventory clients, then prove old JWTs are rejected.

residualRisks: Origin remains directly exposed to Internet abuse at Nginx.
Valid-user application vulnerabilities and authorization mistakes remain.

acceptanceCriteria: Every non-allowlisted anonymous route is denied and every admin route rejects normal users.
migrationNotes: Preserve explicit service-token paths for non-browser clients.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Retain default-deny/private ports and temporarily restore short-lived bearer compatibility if needed.

options.title: Identity-aware edge plus application gate
options.summary: Add MFA edge identity, WAF/bot controls, and origin allowlisting to the full application gate.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Edge and Nginx both deny anonymous HTML.
Application default-deny remains authoritative for routes and roles.
Unsafe application fallback is removed rather than hidden behind the edge.
Edge MFA and bot policy supplement origin account/IP/global limits.
Revocable server sessions remain the browser credential.
Origin and internal services accept only trusted network paths.
Signed edge assertions and origin isolation establish a trustworthy proxy boundary.

tradeoffs.assessment: MFA, bot controls, and origin isolation reduce password and direct-origin attacks before application processing.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test edge bypass, assertion forgery, origin firewall, and MFA recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds an edge network and identity decision hop, partly offset by static caching.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure regional p50/p95 edge-to-origin latency and login flow duration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Origin memory matches app-gate; edge state is provider-owned.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure origin Redis/session state as for app-gate.

tradeoffs.assessment: Improves attack isolation but adds edge/identity-provider failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run edge outage and policy-lockout drills with a private break-glass path.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds provider policy, enrollment, DNS/tunnel, assertion validation, and break-glass ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete operator enrollment, access review, and recovery runbooks.

tradeoffs.assessment: Includes app migration plus edge/network cutover.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Roll out edge observe mode, MFA enrollment, then origin allowlisting.

residualRisks: Authenticated application vulnerabilities and insider misuse.

acceptanceCriteria: Direct origin traffic fails and only enrolled MFA identities reach protected routes.
migrationNotes: Do not restrict origin until health, edge, and recovery paths are validated.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remove edge routing only after enabling a reviewed direct TLS path; keep application gate and private services.

opportunities.recommendation: Use an identity-aware MFA edge plus a complete application default-deny/session boundary.

opportunities.title: Establish actionable security telemetry
opportunities.summary: Emit complete redacted security events and preserve them in an alerting integrity boundary.
opportunities.diagnosis: Current logs are diagnostic streams without complete authentication events, trustworthy caller identity, or off-host integrity.

evidence.claim: Invalid credentials return without a dedicated security event and auth uses a logger not wired to security.log.
The inspected local security stream was empty and had broad read permissions.
Raw forwarding identity and partial redaction can corrupt audit attribution or leak credentials.

desiredInvariants: All security-relevant identity and administrator decisions emit structured correlated events.
No credential or session material reaches any logging sink.
Client identity is derived only from a trusted proxy boundary.
Security evidence is retained off-host with append-only access and collection-health alerts.

options.title: Structured local security audit
options.summary: Create a JSON event schema, trusted identity, central redaction, restricted files, and local alerts.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Auth and privileged events enter one reviewed stream.
Trusted proxy identity and central redaction correct attribution and leakage.
Privileged actions become visible but still require authorization fixes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Provides missing detection evidence but a host compromise can still erase it.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise every event and redaction fixture, then simulate local deletion.

tradeoffs.assessment: JSON serialization, redaction, and local I/O add bounded CPU/I/O.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark throughput and p95 latency with logging on/off.

tradeoffs.assessment: Synchronous local handlers need little retained memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure RSS during authentication bursts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Rotation and disk alerts reduce silent disk exhaustion; file I/O remains a local failure mode.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fill disk threshold and force rotation errors in staging.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires schema, permissions, rotation, alert, and weekly review ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run one complete weekly review and alert response drill.

tradeoffs.assessment: Can be introduced alongside existing logs and consumers.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare old/new event counts before retiring legacy auth messages.

residualRisks: Application-host compromise can alter local evidence.
Exception text may contain unforeseen secrets.

acceptanceCriteria: All required auth/admin events are emitted and credential canaries never reach logs.
migrationNotes: Keep legacy logs until event-count parity is validated.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable noisy alert rules while keeping structured events and redaction.

options.title: Centralized append-only monitoring
options.summary: Forward structured events over authenticated TLS to restricted append-only storage with correlation and alerts.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Complete source events gain off-host integrity and real-time detection.
Trusted attribution and redaction precede transport.
Privileged action anomalies can be correlated, while authorization still must be fixed.

tradeoffs.assessment: Off-host append-only copies resist application-host evidence deletion and support cross-layer detection.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compromise-simulation test local deletion while verifying central retention and alerting.

tradeoffs.assessment: Asynchronous serialization and transport add bounded overhead; remote writes must never block requests.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure throughput, CPU, queue lag, and p95 latency under normal and attack bursts.

tradeoffs.assessment: A bounded queue/spool retains events during collector delay.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Size queue memory/disk at peak event rate and verify drop policy.

tradeoffs.assessment: Improves evidence durability but adds collector and transport failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Stop collector, exhaust bounded queue, recover, and verify telemetry-loss alerts without request hangs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires TLS identity, storage, retention, query access, rule tuning, and on-call ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete alert, retention, access-review, and incident-response drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local schema can roll out first, then forwarding and dashboards in parallel.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Validate count and field parity before central monitoring becomes authoritative.

residualRisks: Collector administrator compromise and alert fatigue.
Missing source instrumentation remains invisible centrally.

acceptanceCriteria: Security events survive host-local deletion and collection silence creates an alert.
migrationNotes: Forward asynchronously with bounded buffering and explicit drop metrics.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Retain local structured audit and disable forwarding without removing source events.

opportunities.recommendation: Build correct local events first, then forward them to an append-only monitored store.

openQuestions: Which identity-aware edge and MFA method will be operated?
Which secret manager or protected deployment store will be authoritative?
Which non-admin accounts should remain active?
Which central security log store, retention, and on-call destination will be used?
Which non-browser clients need service-token compatibility?
